seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p: Metzger Lenz , a more than Velasquez Velázquez figure, meat warrior. He occupied all the tram platform.

The King of Oil’s daughter , born Edith Rockefeller, ill favoured, malsaine fantastic distinguished and benevolent, she stalked about the town distributing charities houses and jachts yachts .
Rossen Rawson
taught her husband McCormick, to whistle the song it ain’t gonna Waltza no more.
She is the daughter of one Rockefeller whose oil brought more death into our world and much of our woe.
Oom Paul Of Niederdorf Ministre de la Grille, Dutch interior mais où sont les Bifteks D’Antan?
L’homme qui rit, He had a lion’s mouth from ear to ear and walked about the bourse with a copious english English newspaper held up to his face.

Juda Devries Dentist thief cinematograf producer (pink not paper with the allied flags crossed on the top) contrabandist in shirtwaists sinthetic synthetic pearls and bouillon Kub. Canary gloves patent shoes. Alias Joe Martin. Alias Jules Moreau, his father the venerable ginecologist gynecologist in Amsterdam; my father got him out of jail in hospital. He wrote a scenario Wine, Woman and Song. While in Prison prison made a wooden Bible money box, a surprise entitled “My first Success” by James Joyce.

Sigmund Feilbogen
Ear trumpet which he oriented and occidented night and day to catch rumours of peace anywhere at any hour. The slings and arrows of outrageous fortune had hit him hard. Said to have lost his proffesorship professorship in the higher school of Commerce in Vienna because his wife (Rubens type with one eye gone West) urged by female curiosity half consumed the host the pope gave her in St. Peter’s and then spat it into her handkerchief.

Zirrizittig Extrablatt All through the War he stood at the corner of the Banhofplatz Bahnhofplatz with a plaster on his chest and distributed Havas Stephanie Reuter and Wolff with Vierwaldstätter je m’en foutisme.
My father sends you the above hints as companion pictures of that of Busoni and his dog. We hope you weathered the storm safely.

div.note: The letter makes suggestions for Budgen’s book that were incorporated into the galley proofs, set probably in August 1933.
Budgen describes these Zurich personalities, at times quoting directly from this letter, in JJMU 26-30.
Jakob Lenz, a Zurich butcher, whom Budgen notes “in girth surpassing Velasquez’s actor”, (JJMU 29) perhaps in reference to the painting “El bufón Barbarroja”.
In JJMU 28 Budgen made reference to Edith Rockefeller's philanthropy, but omitted JJ's caustic comment.
This sentence is written in the left margin in the hand of JJ.

The nickname of Paul Kruger, the president of South Africa during the Boer War, and here a humorous reference to the Dutch Jan Ephraim (“Oom Jan”), owner of the Meierei restaurant in Zurich’s Niederdorf, famous for his grilled steaks. The question echoes the line “Mais où sont les neiges d'antan?” from François Villon’s poem “La Ballade des dames du temps jadis”. As translated by Dante Gabriel Rosetti, “But where are the snows of yesteryear?” the question appears in the Wake as “but wowhere are those yours of Yestersdays?” (FW 54.03).
A reference to the Victor Hugo novel of 1869 published in English under the title The Man Who Laughs.

The incident prompting the loss of his professorship was apparently due to his sister-in-law, not his wife (Andreas Fischer, James Joyce in Zurich: A Guide [Cham: Palgrave Macmillan, 2020], 117). He appears in the Wake as “Father Freeshots Feilbogen” (FW 464.29-30).

A local colloquial reference to the “extra” section of the Neue Zürcher Zeitung, the most prominent newspaper in Zurich during JJ’s time there. JJ used the nickname in a letter to Lucia of 8 August 1932 (LIII 255), and it appears in JJMU as “Zürizitig”. The term “Zürizitig” is still used as a nickname for the newspaper. Havas, Stefani, Reuters, and Wolffs were press agencies located in, respectively, France, Italy, Britain, and Germany. They appear in the Wake (along with others) as “Tass, Patt, Staff, Woff, Havv, Bluvv and Rutter” (FW 593.06). “Vierwaldstättersee” is the German name of Lake Lucerne. “Je m’en foutisme” is the noun form of the French phrase “je m’en fous”, meaning “I don’t care”.

Busoni’s strolls in the company of his St. Bernard dog, “Giotto”, were a familiar sight on Bahnhofstrasse during JJ's years in Zurich. Budgen reported that Busoni would walk to his concerts in Zurich's Tonhalle in the company of the dog (JJMU 26).
